decisions.reason: A safety shoe line is very close to the firm's established footwear knowledge base, so early market learning should be easy to absorb and improve rather than abandon.
A comfort insole for work shoes fits the firm's core capabilities, but as a less prominently presented add-on product it has a somewhat higher risk if demand proves weaker than expected.

A supportive insole is technologically related to the firm's existing work-shoe business, yet overlap with other insole variants makes rationalisation somewhat more likely if initial feedback is mixed.
An ergonomic safety shoe series received strong standalone presentation and builds directly on the firm's accumulated expertise, making continued refinement more likely than withdrawal.

Firefighter and rescue boots are a specialised but still closely related protective-footwear segment, so a large experienced German manufacturer would usually keep them while using early feedback to adapt the offer.
A moulded insole for work shoes was highlighted on the home page and is highly complementary to the firm's core products, which supports retention and further development.
